Question: A line with slope \(3\) intersects a line with slope \(5\) at the point \((10, 15).\) What is the distance between the \(x\)-intercepts of these two lines?
Solution:
An \(x\)-intercept has vertical coordinate \(0\), so the rise from either intercept to \((10,15)\) is \(15\). Both slopes are positive, so both intercepts lie to the left of \((10,15)\).

Slope equals rise divided by horizontal run. Thus the line with slope \(3\) has horizontal run \(15/3=5\), placing its intercept at \((10-5,0)=(5,0)\). The line with slope \(5\) has horizontal run \(15/5=3\), placing its intercept at \((10-3,0)=(7,0)\).

Since both intercepts lie on the \(x\)-axis, their distance is
\[
7-5=\boxed{2},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
